newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Netcomm to spin off cable modem unit.
newsitem.headline: Netcomm to spin off cable modem unit.

text.p: Modem maker NetComm Ltd said on Thursday its cable modem unit Aurora Communications Pty Ltd plans to list on the NASDAQ exchange in the United States but not on the Australian Stock Exchange.

NetComm's cable modem development activities were recently transferred into Aurora to isolate cable modem activities from NetComm's core modern business and to enable Aurora to raise external funding for the continuing development of cable modems.
NetComm earlier unveiled a merger with Banksia Technologies, which would result in Banksia's managing director David Stewart becoming the major shareholder in the merged modem group.
In June 1997, NetComm's shareholders approved Aurora entering into a share subscription and option agreement with NetComm shareholder ADC Telecommunications Inc.

Under this agreement, ADC has an option to subscribe for values representing 19.9 percent of Aurora's total issued capital at a price equal to the value of ADC's shareholding in NetComm, NetComm said.

It said ADC has reached agreement to sell its shareholding in NetComm to David Stewart at a price of 70 cents per share, with 50 percent to be acquired immediately and the remaining 50 percent to be acquired on shareholder approval of the merger.

The proceeds from the share sale, about A$1.8 million, will be directed into Aurora in accordance with the subscription and option agreement and then convert into a 19.9 percent shareholding in Aurora, NetComm said.
This transaction will imply a value of Aurora around A$9.1 million, it said.

Aurora's primary focus has been the development of cable modem devices for use with ADC's Homeworx integrated HFC system. "It is envisaged that Aurora's activities will continue to focus on ADC related products until further funding is raised for non-ADC specific cable modem products," it said.
NetComm shareholders will be provided with a direct investment in Aurora through a distribution of NetComm's shareholding in Aurora.
Through this process, NetComm"s shareholders will be provided with six shares in Aurora for every 11 shares held in NetComm.
At 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT), NetComm shares were 20 cents or 33.33 percent up at 80 cents per share.
